description: §19.8.3 / §19.8.4 (S451 R11) — a `?{}` query handled by `!{}` as the right-hand side of a declaration / assignment in a server function (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"). Three database states in one program: `notes` has a row, `empties` is an empty table, `gone` is declared in <schema> but never created, so a query on it FAILS TO RUN ("no such table"). `.get()` on the row → the row; on the empty table → `not` (no row is not a failure); on the missing table → the `.QueryFailed(m)` arm runs. `.all()` on the missing table → the `_ :> []` arm (length 0). A keywordless reassignment `row = ?{…}.get() !{…}` assigns the existing binding; a parenthesized `( ?{…}.get() !{…} )` lowers like the bare form. Pre-S454 every one of these failed the build with E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC (`let _scrml__scrml_result_N = ;`) — g-sql-handler-arm-on-all-in-fn-statement-emits-empty-assign-s454.
rationale: §19.8.3: "A `?{}` query is a failable expression everywhere"; handling form 1 is "A `!{}` handler on the query — written after the terminator (`.get()`, `.all()`, `.run()`), its arms match `SqlError` variants" with example 1 `const row = ?{…}.get() !{ .QueryFailed(m) :> { …; return "?" } … }`. §19.8.3: "`.get()` on zero rows returns `not`, and `.all()` on zero rows returns `[]` … Only a query that fails to run … produces a `SqlError` variant." §19.4.3 lists the declaration initializer and the assignment right-hand side (`x = f() !{ … }`) as value positions.
